headlineMetrics.label: INPS pensions and allowances in force
headlineMetrics.definition: All current INPS pension benefits in the published stock, including previdenziale and assistenziale benefits. This is not a count of unique people.

headlineMetrics.label: Annualized INPS amount in force
headlineMetrics.definition: January monthly amount multiplied by 13, or by 12 for attendance allowances, under the INPS observatory definition.

headlineMetrics.label: Previdenziale share of current benefits
headlineMetrics.definition: Benefits classified by INPS as previdenziale, mainly contributory old-age, invalidity, and survivor pensions.

headlineMetrics.label: Assistenziale share of current benefits
headlineMetrics.definition: Benefits classified by INPS as assistenziale, including civil invalidity and social pensions or allowances.

headlineMetrics.label: Unique pensioners
headlineMetrics.definition: People receiving at least one pension benefit in the INPS beneficiary observatory.

headlineMetrics.label: INPS contribution revenue
headlineMetrics.definition: Competence-accounted contribution revenue in the INPS General Accounts for 2025.

headlineMetrics.label: INPS pension outlays
headlineMetrics.definition: Institutional pension benefits recorded in the INPS 2025 budget, covering private and public managements.

headlineMetrics.label: State current transfers to INPS
headlineMetrics.definition: Current state transfers in the INPS budget. The GIAS detail totals EUR 165,252 million, with a small reconciliation difference to the broader state-transfer line.

headlineMetrics.label: Projected gross public pension expenditure peak
headlineMetrics.definition: Peak in the 2024 Ageing Report Italy baseline, under its public-pension perimeter and policy assumptions.

headlineMetrics.label: Projected gross public pension expenditure in 2070
headlineMetrics.definition: Official baseline projection. It is not a forecast of a collapse date or a guarantee about future legislation.

headlineMetrics.label: Projected resident population
headlineMetrics.definition: Istat median scenario based on the resident population at 2024-01-01; rounded to one decimal million.

perimeterNotes: The INPS budget reports competence revenues and outlays. It is not the same series as the annualized stock of benefits paid in January or the Eurostat ESSPROS pension function.
GIAS is a state-funded account that records assistance and pension-policy charges. It should not be presented as an unexplained pension shortfall.
The institutional-benefits history is broader than pensions because it includes income support, family benefits, and other services.

spendingProjection.modelVintage: Policy and system information at 2023-09-30; projections finalized in autumn 2023
spendingProjection.unit: percent of GDP unless stated otherwise

sensitivityGrossExpenditureDelta.scenario: higher employment among older workers by 10 percentage points

spendingProjection.perimeterDefinition: The Ageing Report public pension perimeter covers public old-age, survivor, and contribution-related disability pensions, plus some old-age allowances and social supplements. It is slightly below the Eurostat ESSPROS total because some disability, work-injury, war-pension, and other items are outside the model.

medianNetMigrationThousands.qualifier: Istat describes the median path as below 200 thousand per year

interpretationNotes: The Istat old-age dependency ratio is residents aged 65 and over divided by residents aged 15 to 64, multiplied by 100.
Istat and the Ageing Report use different population vintages, age bands, and projection models. Their values should be compared directionally, not merged into one series.

inpsStock2026.perimeter: INPS current stock, including GDP public employees and assistential benefits, excluding former INPGI in the cited report

beneficiaryObservatory2024.definition: Pensioner income sums all benefits received by a person, regardless of whether the benefit is previdenziale, indennitario, or assistenziale.

interpretationNotes: The 2026 INPS stock counts benefits. The 2024 beneficiary observatory counts both benefits and unique people, so 23.015 million benefits and 16.306 million pensioners are not contradictory.
Category counts in the multiple-benefit tables overlap because one pensioner can belong to several benefit categories.
A benefit amount band is not a person income band. A pensioner income band sums every benefit received by that person.

In the 2024 beneficiary data, 53.9 percent of benefits were below EUR 1,000 per month, while 28.1 percent of unique pensioners had total pension income below EUR 1,000. The difference is mainly a multiple-benefit and unit-of-count issue.

The INPS report says that only 42.2 percent of benefits at or below EUR 749.99 were linked to low-income provisions in its defined set. A low benefit amount alone does not establish household poverty or a policy error.
A high amount band records an administrative distribution. It does not establish abuse, illegality, or an unfair award.
These category rows overlap. Their pensioner counts and benefits cannot be added to obtain a national total.
Cumulation can be legally designed, for example an old-age pension with a survivor pension or a benefit linked to invalidity. The table describes combinations, not abuse.

The 2024 report found that 27.7 percent of old-age pensioners, 46.0 percent of contributory-invalidity pensioners, 68.3 percent of survivor pensioners, 71.5 percent of indennitarie pensioners, and 48.2 percent of assistenziale pensioners received at least one other type.

payg.text: Italy has a mandatory public pay-as-you-go system. Current contributions and state transfers finance current benefits; the public system is not a personal investment account.

For the notional defined-contribution part, lifetime contributions are capitalized at nominal GDP growth using a five-year moving average and multiplied by a transformation coefficient linked to mortality and remaining life expectancy.

A defined-benefit formula applies pro rata to contributions before the relevant 1995 or 2011 transition dates, depending on contribution history. People starting after 1 January 1996 are fully in the contributory calculation.
Statutory retirement ages and transformation coefficients are linked to life expectancy, subject to legislative freezes, exemptions, and timing rules.

contributionRates.group: average earner effective mandatory contribution rate
contributionRates.qualifier: OECD comparison includes mandatory public pension contributions and may include disability or invalidity coverage; tax-financed benefits are excluded

retirementRequirements.qualifier: Not extended for new maturities; available only to people who had met the requirements by 2025-12-31
Extended through 2026 for eligible categories; it is not an ordinary old-age pension

transitionMechanisms.qualifier: Mixed pro-rata rules apply during the transition; full contributory calculation applies to people starting after 1995
The link was frozen for 2019 to 2026 and exemptions apply to specified strenuous or night work categories

over 4 and up to 5 times the minimum pension

indexationMechanism.warning: The fiche also records temporary 2023 to 2024 bands. Do not present this long-run assumption as a complete year-specific calculation for every current pension.

uncertainty: The Ageing Report baseline holds policy rules and macro-demographic assumptions in a specific model vintage. Later legislation, migration, fertility, employment, productivity, inflation, and life expectancy can move the outcome.
The official sensitivity table reports changes in gross pension expenditure relative to the baseline. It does not provide a probability distribution.
A declining expenditure share after the projected 2036 peak reflects the model path and demographic transition. It is not evidence of an inevitable collapse or a policy recommendation.

methodologyNotes.text: Every series is marked as observed, official_baseline, official_projection, or derived. Values from an official model are not observations, even when the year is in the past.

The 2026 INPS observatory counts benefits in force at 2026-01-01 and annualizes the January amount. It includes previdenziale and assistenziale benefits, and this edition includes GDP public employees.
The 2024 INPS beneficiary observatory reports 23.015 million benefits and 16.306 million unique pensioners. Its pensioner income bands sum all benefits received by each person.

The 2025 INPS General Accounts are competence accounts. Current revenues, transfers, pension outlays, institutional benefits, and GIAS should not be read as a single cash-flow statement for the whole Italian public sector.

Eurostat ESSPROS, OECD public cash expenditure, INPS administrative accounts, and the Ageing Report public-pension perimeter differ in functions, institutions, timing, and inclusion of assistance. The same year can therefore have different valid percentages.
A person can receive several benefits. Benefit counts, category pensioner counts, and unique pensioner counts must never be added without checking overlap.
Monthly bands describe January benefit amounts in the INPS stock report or annualized pension income in the beneficiary report. They are not equivalent measures.
Derived ratios are simple arithmetic on published values and are rounded only for display. They do not allocate state transfers across individual benefits or estimate an implicit return.
The 2070 path is conditional on the Ageing Report model vintage and assumptions. Use the sensitivity data for scenario context and do not publish a deterministic collapse date.
Multiple-benefit combinations are a normal feature of a system with old-age, survivor, invalidity, indennitarie, and assistenziale programs. The data alone do not show abuse.
Shares and amounts can differ by 0.1 from totals because the official reports round percentages and some amounts to millions.
